answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that vests slowly, like a glacier releasing meltwater: the stake only becomes usable after a long voyage of verified work, so an attacker spawning thousands of sock-puppets must lock up capital for every single one. Pair that with a crystal-clear public reputation ledger where each completed task adds a verifiable entry; a fresh identity with no history cannot outbid established agents, and faking history costs real fees per entry, making mass fakery uneconomic.
